extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, patent agents, and parties participating in PTAB appeals and AIA trials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on scheduling, format selection, public access, health/safety protocols, and special programs for PTAB hearings (virtual and in-person) following pandemic changes. Advises parties how to request hearing formats, timelines for Board communications, and facility-access rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of hearing formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtual hearings will continue for appeals and AIA trials. No in-person hearings unless requested by both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virtual is the default/continued option; in-person hearings are available only when both parties request them.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-person hearing timing (important dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: The option for in-person hearings will be available for hearings scheduled on or after July 11, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO officially reopened to the public on May 25, 2022; in-person option applies to hearings scheduled on or after the stated date.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request a preferred hearing option
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties can request virtual or in-person hearing at initial conference, in a separate filing with the Board, or in their request for oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parties don’t express a preference for virtual or in-person, the Board will email parties to determine preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board email to determine preferences (timeline and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: If parties haven’t made their preferences known, parties should expect an email from Trials@USPTO.gov about 6–8 weeks before the scheduled hearing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email will ask parties to inform the Board (1) whether the parties would prefer either a virtual hearing or an in-person hearing and (2) for in-person hearings, which of the locations (as offered by the Scheduling Order) the parties would prefer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to hearings (primary means and restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remote access will continue for PTAB hearings, either by video or audio. This is the primary means for public access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to availability of space, in-person public access may also be granted; includes designated hearing location and alternate sites. Public access not available for hearings with confidential information. For virtual or in-person access to a hearing, submit a request to PTABHearings@uspto.gov at least 3 days before the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to obtain public hearing schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing schedules are posted on the PTAB page of the USPTO website at https://www.uspto.gov/patents/ptab/hearings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PTAB website hearings page to find scheduled hearings and access information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arguing counsel in-person appearance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguing counsel may appear in person from any location with an APJ present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most in-person hearings will still likely have one or more judges attending the hearing virtually; parties who are no longer able to appear in-person should contact PTABHearings@uspto.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-arguing personnel attendance recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-arguing personnel are encouraged to attend remotely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when in-person hearings occur, non-arguing staff should plan to attend virtually to limit on-site presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing USPTO facilities — reference and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on access to USPTO facilities can be found at https://www.uspto.gov/coronavirus — community transmission levels, safety protocols, self-certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules apply to any person accessing USPTO facilities and should be consulted prior to planning in-person attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community transmission levels and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: CDC COVID-19 Community Levels are applied to each USPTO location. Information is updated every Friday and applies for one week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community levels can be low, medium, or high and determine applicable safety protocols for each location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety protocols tied to community levels (masking rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO safety protocols correspond to the CDC Community Level for that location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In communities with low or medium transmission levels, masks are optional. In communities with high transmission levels, wearing a mask in our buildings is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-certification health questionnaire requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Visitors should review self-certification health questionnaire prior to entering and may not enter USPTO facilities if they answer 'yes' to any of the questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this makes attending a scheduled in-person hearing impossible, contact PTABHearings@uspto.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and question contact
rubrics_metrics.description: To send in questions or comments during the webinar, please email PTABBoardsideChat@uspto.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The slide repeats this contact for webinar Q&A; similar contacts are provided for hearing logistics (PTABHearings@uspto.gov) and scheduling emails (Trials@USPTO.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of virtual hearings (factors favoring virtual format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Saves time and money; Positive environmental impact; Easy sharing of demonstratives; APJs appear virtually, regardless of location; Easier access for interested parties who are not giving oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These benefits are cited as reasons virtual hearings may be preferable for parties and the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEAP qualification criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for the Legal Experience and Advancement Program (LEAP), a patent agent or attorney must have three or fewer substantive oral arguments in any federal tribunal, including PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAP is designed to aid development of new patent practitioners and encourage a diverse group of advocates to develop skills before the PTAB.
